contract.name: curriculum-runtime-v1
contract.what: The exact pre-Stage-4 semantics of the three hand-authored curriculum runtime files.
contract.why: Stage 4 makes src/data/modules.js, src/chapters.js and src/content/chapterContentRegistry.js re-export the generated projections. From that commit on, comparing the generated files with those three files compares the generated files with themselves. This fixture is the independent side of the comparison: it is what the runtime meant BEFORE the cutover, captured once and never regenerated from the runtime again.

provenance.capturedWhen: Stage 3 → Stage 4 boundary, while all three files were still hand-authored.

contract.authority: NOT authority. This is a frozen migration contract, not a curriculum source and not a compatibility source. It is test-only: no production module and no generator may read it. The curriculum authority is src/curriculum-catalogue/records/**; the legacy-interface authority is src/curriculum-catalogue/compatibility/runtime-v1.js.
contract.editing: Editing this file is editing the migration contract. Any edit must be a deliberate, reviewed statement that the pre-cutover runtime is now understood differently — never a way to make a failing parity test pass. tests/architecture/curriculum-projection-parity.test.js pins its checksum, so an edit here fails until the checksum is updated in the same change.
contract.retirement: Delete this fixture at Stage 6, in the same change that deletes src/curriculum-catalogue/compatibility/. Its whole job is to prove the generated projections still reproduce the legacy interface; once no legacy runtime consumer and no compatibility field remain, there is no legacy interface left to reproduce and nothing for it to prove. It must not outlive compatibility/ — a frozen contract with no counterparty is dead weight that will silently start describing something else.
